title: Class of a frame
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $n\geq1$, $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda=A$. Let $V\to B$ be a smooth morphism of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of $k$-schemes, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], of pure codimension $c\geq0$, with $Z\to B$ smooth. Here pure codimension means $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+c$ for every $z\in Z$, with Krull dimension the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals.

A *frame at $Z$* consists of an etale morphism $e:U\to V$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and an ordered tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ generating the ideal sheaf of the closed subscheme $Z_U:=Z\times_VU$ [def-pc-base-change]. Thus $Z_U$ is the closed subscheme locally defined by $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. In the source, the expressions "etale open" and $Z\cap U$ mean this etale neighbourhood and this fibre product; $e$ need not be an open immersion. For each $j$, put $D_j=V(f_j)\hookrightarrow U$, the closed subscheme locally defined by the principal ideal $(f_j)$, and $W_j=U\setminus D_j$, its complementary open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. On $W_j$, $f_j$ is a unit: on each affine chart this is the element $f_j$ of the localization $R_{f_j}$, with inverse $1/f_j$.

Use the small pro-etale site and its constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], supported cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology], the finite-level twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The following specifies the concrete Kummer class of any unit $u$ on a $k$-scheme $W$, including coefficient indices not divisible by the ramification index. Put $m=\ell^n$ and $R=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$; $m$ is invertible on $W$ and $mA=0$, since $\ell\in(\varpi_E)$. Let $M_W=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_W=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r,W}$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](2), its projection induces $M_W/mM_W\cong\mu_{m,W}$. The twist definition and tensor associativity identify
$$
 A(1)_W
 = (M_W\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathcal O_E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}A
 \cong M_W\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}A
 \cong (M_W/mM_W)\otimes_R A
 \cong\mu_{m,W}\otimes_R A.
$$
All rings in these sheaf tensors mean their constant sheaves. The quotient $M_W/mM_W$ is also the tensor of $M_W$ with $R_W$ over the completed coefficient sheaf: both are the cokernel of multiplication by $m$ on $M_W$. Consequently clause (2) of the cited lemma applies to this quotient. Write $\pi_n:M_W\to\mu_{m,W}$ for the inverse-limit projection and $\theta_W:A(1)_W\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{m,W}\otimes_RA$ for this projection-induced identification, characterized by $\theta_W(z\otimes a)=\pi_n(z)\otimes a$ on local tensor generators. Define $\sigma_W:\mu_{m,W}\to A(1)_W$ by $v\mapsto\theta_W^{-1}(v\otimes1_A)$.

On $W_{\mathrm{et}}$, use the exact Kummer sequence of [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] (Stacks Tag 03PL, etale-cohomology, lemma-kummer-sequence), with units sheaf $\mathbf G_{m,W}$ as in [def-sc-gm-torsor]. Write $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,W}=\ker([m]:\mathbf G_{m,W}\to\mathbf G_{m,W})$. Its connecting map, in the right-derived-global-sections convention of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], is
$$
 \delta_W:\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times
 \longrightarrow H^1(W_{\mathrm{et}},\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,W}).
$$
Let $\nu_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}\to W_{\mathrm{et}}$ be [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. On every etale $T\to W$, the identical root formulas define a morphism $\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,W}\to\nu_{W,*}\mu_{m,W}$, where the pro-etale root sheaf is [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Denote its adjoint by $\rho_W:\nu_W^{-1}\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,W}\to\mu_{m,W}$. Write $\operatorname{comp}_W:H^1(W_{\mathrm{et}},\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,W})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_W^{-1}\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{m,W})$ for the canonical cohomology comparison of [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison]. Applying cohomology to the abelian-sheaf morphism $\sigma_W\circ\rho_W$ then defines
$$
 \kappa_W(u)=H^1(\sigma_W\circ\rho_W)\bigl(\operatorname{comp}_W(\delta_W(u))\bigr)
 \in H^1(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1)_W).
$$
This is the Kummer-boundary prescription used in [def-pur-affine-line-datum], now specified for every $n\geq1$; it extends coefficients on the roots sheaf, not on $\mathbf G_m$ as an $R$-module.

For each $j$, take the boundary of the individual closed-open pair $(U,D_j)$ supplied by [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], with coefficient sheaf $A(1)_U$:
$$
 \partial_j:H^1((W_j)_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1)_{W_j})
 \longrightarrow H^2_{D_j}(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A(1)_U),
 \qquad \alpha_j=\partial_j\kappa_{W_j}(f_j|_{W_j}).
$$
Restriction of the twist to $W_j$ is read through its defining roots and tensors. Define the *class of the frame* by the ordered, left-associated supported cup product of [def-pur-supported-cup]:
$$
 \operatorname{cl}(f)=\alpha_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha_c
 \in H^{2c}_{Z_U}(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A(c)_U).
$$
For $c=0$, the ideal generated by the empty tuple is zero, so $Z_U=U$; the empty product means the unit $1\in H^0_U(U,A)=H^0(U,A)$. For $c>0$, the scheme-theoretic intersection $D_1\times_U\cdots\times_UD_c$ is $Z_U$: on an affine chart its ideal is the sum $(f_1)+\cdots+(f_c)$. Each cup product adds the cohomological degrees and tensors the coefficient sheaves, so the resulting degree is $2c$ and the coefficient is $A(1)^{\otimes_A c}=A(c)$. The line sheaves are locally free by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], so these tensors agree with the derived tensors used by the supported cup product [def-weil-derived-tensor]. No independence of the frame, existence of frames, or purity isomorphism is part of this definition.

proof.text: The range of a tuple of length d+1 is the union of its prefix range and its last singleton (Fin.lastCases). Ideal.span_union identifies the generated ideals. Apply the already proved Scheme.isPullback_zeroLocusSubschemeι_union and take its canonical isoPullback. Its equation over X follows from isoPullback_hom_fst and IdealSheafData.inclusion_subschemeι. The intersection immersion is monic, so cancellation proves uniqueness. The selected isomorphism satisfies its equation by choose_spec.

For an empty tuple, factor the identity of X through its zero subscheme by liftZeroLocusSubscheme; its vanishing condition is vacuous. Monicity supplies the other inverse equation. For any isomorphism c, its pro-etale pullback functor is naturally isomorphic to the over-map along inv c, hence cocontinuous. The constant-sheaf adjunction identifies cupCoefficientRestriction with the pushforward/sheafification compatibility isomorphism, conjugated by cupConstantIso. It is therefore invertible, including for the empty scheme.

Integer casts distribute over addition, and multiplication by two distributes over d+1, giving frameDegreeNext. Retain the specified ordered recursive product. Express its tensor comparison through frameSingleTensorMap (the existing cupDerivedCoefficientMap with an explicitly named single functor), and use supportedCup on the same single objects with their degree-zero lower bounds proved explicitly. These presentations are definitionally equal to the originals. frameFold is the same dependent Nat.rec with its result family abstract; specializing it gives exactly the original frameBoundaryProduct recurrence. frameSingleUnit implements the same mapped inverse coefficient restriction and zero-shift comparison, after substituting the coefficient equality in the generic sheaf category; its objects are explicit in frameEmptyClass.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$A=A_{E,n}$, let $V\to B$ be smooth of relative dimension $n$ and
let $Z\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed subfamily of pure codimension $c$
with $Z\to B$ smooth. A *frame at $Z$* is an etale open
$U\to V$ together with functions $f_1,\dots,f_c\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$
generating the ideal of $Z\cap U$. Put $D_j=V(f_j)$; the function
$f_j$ is a unit on $U\setminus D_j$. Use the boundary for this
individual closed–open pair from [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]
to define $\alpha_j=\partial_j\kappa(f_j)\in H^2_{D_j}(U,\Lambda(1))$.
The *class of the frame* is their
supported cup product

$$
\operatorname{cl}(f)
\;=\;\alpha_1\cup\cdots\cup\alpha_c
\;\in\;H^{2c}_{Z\cap U}\bigl(U,\Lambda(c)\bigr),
$$

where the Kummer classes are those of
[def-pur-affine-line-datum].

Each factor $\alpha_j$ has degree two and twist one; their supports
intersect in $Z\cap U$, giving degree $2c$ and twist $c$.
